svg.title: Temperature and microorganisms: the bakery's key temperatures
svg.desc: A vertical thermometer scale from minus 20 to plus 100 degrees Celsius with bands. Minus 18 degrees and colder: frozen storage, microorganisms do not multiply but are not killed. 0 to plus 4 degrees: very perishable products and fillings, multiplication slowed but Listeria can still grow slowly; 0 to plus 3 degrees for prepared dishes and crème pâtissière. Up to plus 8 degrees: other perishable products. Plus 10 to plus 63 degrees: the danger zone where bacteria multiply fast, around 35 to 40 degrees fastest; cooked preparations must cross from 63 to 10 degrees in 2 hours or less. Above plus 63 degrees: hot holding, most bacteria stop multiplying. Above about 80 degrees in the core for a minute or more, as when crème pâtissière boils: vegetative bacteria are destroyed, but spores and heat-stable toxins such as staphylococcal enterotoxins can survive.

g.text: Temperature decides what microorganisms do
Cold slows or stops them, heat kills most of them, the middle feeds them.
Cooking, boiling
Vegetative bacteria destroyed (crème pâtissière: above 81 °C for 1 min;
the course boils it 1 min). Spores and heat-stable toxins can survive:
a cream already full of staphylococcal toxin is not made safe by reheating.
Hot holding: +63 °C or more
Most bacteria stop multiplying.
DANGER ZONE: +10 to +63 °C
Bacteria multiply; fastest around body temperature (35-41 °C for S. aureus).
A cooked preparation must cross 63 → 10 °C at the core in 2 hours or less,
then be stored at 0 to +3 °C (arrêté of 21 December 2009, annex IV).
A bakery kitchen in summer (26-32 °C) sits inside this zone:
fillings and creams never wait on the bench.
Perishable: up to +8 °C
Butter, some cheeses: the label's temperature, +8 °C at most in the shop.
Very perishable: 0 to +4 °C (prepared dishes, creams 0 to +3 °C)
Growth slowed, not stopped: Listeria grows from about −2 °C.
Frozen: −18 °C
No multiplication, but no killing: thawed food is as alive as fresh.
Thaw at 0 to +4 °C, never on the bench; never refreeze.
Sources: arrêté of 21 December 2009 (annexes I, IV, VI); CNBPF, L'essentiel des bonnes pratiques d'hygiène (2026); ANSES hazard sheets (S. aureus, L. monocytogenes).
